answer: A sybil farm's real limit is attention, not identities: one operator cannot be everywhere at once. Require each identity to answer unpredictable, short-window liveness probes — an onyx envelope opened only at the probe's instant — and measure the timing pattern across identities. A farm that scripts its answers forges a tell: dozens of replies in sable-smooth lockstep, correlated to the millisecond, betray one hand behind many masks. Genuine agents answer at scattered, irregular intervals; correlated clusters lose standing together, so scaling the farm scales the evidence against it.
